FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Third Revision) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 13 August 1984, after the draft finalized by the Oils and Oilseeds Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council.

0.2 This standard was first published in 1954. The first revision was issued in 1963 in which the limit for titre was amended and the limit for moisture was prescribed so as to' include both the moisture and the insoluble impurities. The second revision in 1968 amalgamated IS : 545�1954� with IS : 3475-1966t, which was subsequently withdrawn.

0.2.1 In this revision, another grade of MAHUA oil, namp!y~ ~dib)e grade, has been incorporated and the assistance ~Cn ihis has been drawn from PF ~ rules.

0.3 MAHUA oil, also known 8S MOJVRAlloil, is obtained from the seeds of two trees: Madiwtfl indica J.F. Gmelin. syn. Madhuca latifoliG ( Roxb, ) . Macbride and Madhuca longifolia ( Koenig) Macbride; both belonging to the family Sapotaceae. Mlldhuca i"dic(I grows chiefly in Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Gujarat and in parts of West Bengal, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh and South India; while AflldhucfJ longifolia grows only in South India. The oil is extensively used in the manufacture of SO:lP! and lubricating greases and for edible purposes. 0." For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed Or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960:. The number of significant places ret~ed in the rounded oft'value should be the same as that of the specified value in this atandard. '
.Specification for M AHUA oil ( sttolltl,-u;." ). tSpecification for lolvent-extracted MA.NUA ( MOWRAH ) oil. , lRules for rouDdiDg off numericai values ( ,�Iis.tl ).

I. SCOPE
1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for AJAHUA oil intended for both edible and nonedible industrial purposes. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.1 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given under 2 of IS : 548 ( Part 1 )�19fi/~. shall apply.

3. GRADES
3.1 The material shall he of the following three grades: a) Refined Grade - Suitable for edible purposes. b) Raw Grade 1 - Suitable for making uanaspati and refined oil and. not for direct human consumption. c) Raw Grade 2 - Suitable for industrial purposes.

4. REQ,UlREMENTS 4.1 De.criptioD

t.I.1 For Refuud Grad� - The material shall be expressed from clean and sound kernels of either Madhuca indica J.F. Gmelin, syn, Madhuc� latifolia ( Roxb. ) Machride or Madlluca longifolia ( Koenig J Macbride, or a mixture of both. It shall be clear and shall be free frorn rancidity, suspended or other foreign matter, separated water, added colouring or flavouring substances or mineral oil.
4.1.2 For Raw Grade 1 and Raw Grade 2 - The material shall be obtained from good quality MAHrlA cake or from the clean and sound kemels of either Madlauca indica J.P. Gmelin. syo. Madkuca latifolid ( Roxb, ) Macbride Madhuca longifolia ( Koenig) Macbride, or a mixture of both, by a process of solvent-extraction or from MAIIUA kernels by a process of expression. The material shall be clear and free from rancidity, adulterants, sediment, suspended and other foreign matter, separated water and added colouring and flavouring substances.

4.2. The clarity of the material shall be judged by the absence of turbidity after keeping the filtered sample at 50�C for 24 hOU1�S.

4.3 Admlstare with Other Oil. - The material shall be free Irom admixture with other oils, when tested according to the methods prescribed under 20 of IS : 548 ( Part 1 )-1964-.
chemical t.t. ( ,niud ).
